summary: John's 7th-great-grandmother, mother of Keturah Tuttle; a granddaughter of Job Smith and great-granddaughter of Richard 'Bull' Smith, founder of Smithtown.
bio: Temperance is the link that carries the whole Smith, Thompson, Topping, Hammond and Paine ancestry. Pelletreau's appendix (p. 479) says James Smith 'settled in Moriches' and married Jerusha Topping, and lists their children as Matthew (b. 1721), Ezekiel, Zebulon, Austin, Nathaniel, Francis, Eunice, Keturah, Temperance and Jeremiah. Temperance Tuttle named her eldest known daughter Keturah (after her sister) and a son Ezekiel (after her brother); Keturah in turn named children James (1774), Temperance (1778) and Keturah (1791). Two of her brothers, Capt. Francis Smith and Capt. Austin Smith, commanded the Woodbury Clove and Upper Clove militia companies in Orange County in 1775–76, with her son-in-law Thomas Lamoreaux as ensign under Francis. Earlier research had a rival candidate: Ebenezer Smith (son of Richard 2d) whose will of 25 Jul 1747 (proved 7 Jan 1747 O.S.; Pelletreau p. 46) left £100 each to 'my daughters Temperance Anna and Hannah' when 21, with wife Anna daughter of Job Smith 2d (p. 472). Pelletreau's appendix (pp. 465, 475) says twice that this Temperance married Jonas Platt and died 12 Mar 1813 his widow, so she cannot be Mrs. Tuttle; that candidacy is closed. Job Smith 2d's daughter Temperance (b. 1714) is about 20 years too early. A chronology question was raised (Jerusha's father 'died in 1705') and resolved in Round 1: Jerusha's father was the younger Elnathan Topping (1664–1751), not Capt. Elnathan (d. 1705). No grave found. A full-text search of Pelletreau found no Tuthill/Tuttle tied to her.
